findings.issue_text: align-items() mixin in mixins.scss:117 passes flex-start/flex-end unchanged to legacy -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, which require start/end, so calls like align-items(flex-start) emit invalid legacy declarations and old WebKit/IE10 fall back to stretch; the mixin should map those values

.panel in header.scss:37 relies on margin-left: auto to right-align, but auto margins are not honored in the 2009 -webkit-box/-moz-box model targeted by the flexbox() mixin, so in those browsers the panel sits after the title instead of right-aligned (regression from float: right); drop the 2009 syntax or add a box-flex spacer/box-pack fallback

order() mixin in mixins.scss:125 maps $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, which is 1-based and rejects 0 or negatives while order is 0-based and accepts negatives, so order(0) or order(-1) produce invalid legacy declarations and inconsistent ordering; document the constraint or offset the legacy value
-ms-align-items in mixins.scss:120 is not a real property in any IE version (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, IE11 uses unprefixed align-items) and is dead output; remove it

.valign-helper in header.scss:21 is still emitted but is now an empty flex item inside a centred flex container, making it dead layout that can contribute inline whitespace width; remove it from the stylesheet and template

.small-action-desc in topic-post.scss:280 had its 4em left padding removed but has no flex: 1/min-width: 0, and .topic-avatar has no fixed flex-basis, so long description text can shrink the avatar column; set .topic-avatar { flex: 0 0 auto } and .small-action-desc { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0 }

PR title 'Optimize header layout performance' is misleading: the change is a float-to-flexbox layout/compat refactor with no measured performance benefit; the description should state the actual goal (vertical centring / ordering)

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() mixin in mixins.scss:117 passes flex-start/flex-end unchanged to legacy -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, which require start/end, so calls like align-items(flex-start) emit invalid legacy declarations and old WebKit/IE10 fall back to stretch; the mixin should map those values

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that writes legacy declarations `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` unchanged. For legacy flexbox syntaxes those properties expect values like `start`/`end` (not `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so if the mixin is called with `flex-start`/`flex-end` it will emit invalid legacy declarations, potentially changing alignment in older WebKit/IE10. While this diff’s usages are `center`/`baseline`, the mixin as added is still defective for common inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .panel in header.scss:37 relies on margin-left: auto to right-align, but auto margins are not honored in the 2009 -webkit-box/-moz-box model targeted by the flexbox() mixin, so in those browsers the panel sits after the title instead of right-aligned (regression from float: right); drop the 2009 syntax or add a box-flex spacer/box-pack fallback

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.contents` is switched to `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` is right-aligned via `margin-left: auto` (replacing `float: right`). The `flexbox()` mixin explicitly emits the 2009 `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` syntax, where auto margins are not a reliable/right-alignment mechanism the way they are in modern flexbox. Given the mixin targets those legacy implementations, this change can regress layout there (panel no longer pushed to the far right).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` in `header.scss` is changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and `.valign-helper` selector still exists, but the diff does not show the `.valign-helper` rule contents, its HTML/template usage, or that it is “empty”/unused. adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action-desc in topic-post.scss:280 had its 4em left padding removed but has no flex: 1/min-width: 0, and .topic-avatar has no fixed flex-basis, so long description text can shrink the avatar column; set .topic-avatar { flex: 0 0 auto } and .small-action-desc { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0 }

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) in `topic-post.scss`, but does not define any flex behavior for its children (`.topic-avatar` / `.small-action-desc`). In flex layouts, the default `flex: 0 1 auto` can allow items (including an avatar container) to shrink under constrained width, and lacking `min-width: 0` on a text block can cause awkward overflow/shrink behavior with long text. The suggested `flex`/`min-width` adjustments are a concrete, diff-grounded layout robustness improvement, but the actual breakage (avatar shrinking) cannot be definitively verified from this diff alone without seeing the DOM/other CSS.
